title: "Find the misalignments" marks every inconsistent edge, padding and gap on a screenshot
goal: A person opens a UI screenshot, asks 'find the misalignments', and Photonz marks what a sharp-eyed designer would: edges that almost line up but miss, padding or border widths that differ between things that should match, and gaps in a repeated pattern that are not equal. Each mark says what is off and by how much, and nothing that is fine gets marked.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20: 'i would love to say "Find the misalignments" on a ux that has inconsistent alignment on things, or inconsistent border/padding widths or gaps in between repeated patterns. I can spot these visually, but i would love the model to be really good at adding annotations for the inconsistent ux things.' This is the user's main use of Photonz (UX redlining).

What exists: find_elements (Sources/PhotonzCore/AgentTools.swift) returns the Measure tool's boxes; ElementBounds.swift, EdgeMap.swift, EdgeRun.swift, MeasurePlan.swift, MeasureSizeGroup.swift, MeasureLabelPlacement.swift (placement that keeps readouts off what they measure). Retina screenshots are 2x: report points, decide 1 pt faults on pixel evidence. Text: compare baselines and cap heights, not box tops, since glyph boxes vary. Do not let the model guess numbers; every number shown comes from the code. The earlier Ask measurement crowding (ask-on-the-local-model-makes-results-that-look-f) is a related task; reuse its placement fixes.
acceptance: Detection is code, not the model: from the boxes the Measure tool finds (and the edges under them), group things that should agree (a column of left edges, a row of tops or baselines or centres, the cards of a repeated list, the insides of matching controls) and flag the ones that miss by 1 to 8 points, the gaps in a run that differ, and padding or border widths that differ between siblings. The model only chooses what is worth showing, words it, and answers follow-ups

Measured on test screenshots with KNOWN planted faults: at least 20 pictures (made from real app and web UIs with offsets of 1, 2 and 3 points, uneven gaps, one card with different padding, a 1 vs 2 point border) where the right answer is written down. Precision and recall go in the audit, each at least 0.9 on the 2 to 3 point faults and at least 0.75 on 1 point; clean screenshots get no more than one false mark

Each finding is a redline annotation in the app's own measurement look: the two edges or gaps compared, both numbers ('16 vs 18'), and a short label ('Gap 2 pt wider than the others'); a group's agreeing members get a quiet guide line so the outlier reads at once; marks never sit over what they point at
The findings are one Ask change row ('Found 6 misalignments') with the usual switch and delete, and each mark is its own layer you can delete
'Find the misalignments' and close phrasings ('check the spacing', 'what is inconsistent here') route to it at Next defaults; on a screenshot with nothing wrong it says so in one short sentence
Works through the Photonz skill too, so an outside agent can run the same check

Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after pictures for five real screenshots, the precision and recall table, and timings. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not
